answer.rationale: The write-path latency climb began ~30 minutes after the release shipped 2 hours ago, making the new build the leading suspect; memory_b1 shows rollback cleared a similar post-release spike without customer impact. However, settlement peak write volume is a plausible alternative cause (memory_b3), so I am verifying memory_b1 before committing and treating the rollback as a guarded, monitored action rather than assuming causality. Rollback preserves customer writes (no data loss from reverting code) and directly maximizes sustained availability if the release is the cause; if latency does not recover post-rollback, add_capacity is the queued next-window intervention.
